questions.prompt: Which race has drawn more outside money so far in the general election?
Can a corporation give unlimited money to a super PAC?
questions.why: Since Citizens United and SpeechNow.org (2010), corporations, unions and individuals can give super PACs unlimited sums.

questions.prompt: In the final 60 days, who pays less for the same TV spot?
questions.why: Stations must sell candidates airtime at the lowest unit charge. Outside groups pay market rates, which climb near Election Day.

questions.prompt: Lower Costs Now (a super PAC) has spent $699K in the KS Senate race. Which party is it helping?
questions.why: Its spending supports the Democrat or attacks their opponent. Every group's filings list who it backs or opposes.

questions.prompt: COMMITTEE FOR AMERICAN LEADERSHIP (a super PAC) has spent $481K in AR's 2nd District House race. Which party is it helping?
questions.why: Its spending supports the Republican or attacks their opponent. Every group's filings list who it backs or opposes.

questions.prompt: What starts the clock on a 24- or 48-hour spending report?
questions.why: The reporting clock starts on the dissemination date, when the ad first reaches the public.

questions.prompt: In NY's 3rd District House race, outside money favors Republicans by $6.3M. Whose nominee has raised more?
questions.why: Outside money and candidate money point opposite ways here: the Democrat leads fundraising by $3.8M.

questions.prompt: Groups helping Democrats have spent $5.6M in CA's 22nd District House race. Are Democrats playing offense or defense?
questions.why: Republicans hold this seat now, so money helping Democrats here is offense.
